header: ## 2-2-2: TERMINATION – SUSPENSION WITHOUT PAY, OR INVOLUNTARY TRANSFER – APPEAL PROCEDURE:

A. Prohibited Employment Practice: An employee may not be terminated, suspended without pay, or involuntarily transferred to a position with less remuneration (demoted):

1. Because of the employee’s politics or religious belief; or

2. Incident to or through changes, either in the elected officials or heads of departments.

B. Applicability:

1. A merit employee who is terminated, suspended for more than two (2) days without pay, or involuntarily transferred from one (1) position to another with less remuneration (demoted) for any disciplinary reason, may appeal the action in writing to an administrative law judge by filing the written appeal and all relevant materials with the city recorder within the timelines and under the general guidelines set forth below and the provisions of the city personnel policies including all future amendments, deletions and additions made by the city.

2. Merit employees who have been dismissed, terminated, separated from employment, or reassigned to a position with less remuneration, based on the employee’s inability to perform the essential functions of the position based upon a medical condition, may appeal that determination to the administrative law judge. The administrative law judge may request the appointment of an independent medical expert, in the administrative law judge’s discretion, if the administrative law judge believes the expert’s opinion is necessary for the resolution of the case.

3. No appeal is allowed for termination or involuntary reassignment due to loss of state or federal licensure or certification which is required for the employee’s position.

C. Process: An employee shall submit a written appeal to the city recorder within ten (10) business days of the disciplinary action. The appeal must be received no later than five o’clock (5:00) P.M. on the tenth business day. At all times during the appeal process, the appealing employee has the right to be represented by legal counsel if they choose.

*Sale or sell* refers to a sale of malt beverages or wine at retail, or to sell such malt beverages or wine at retail, under a license issued under this article.

*Satisfactory proof* means adequate or sufficient evidence to convince an unbiased, impartial, enlightened judge of the existence or nonexistence of a fact, situation or condition.

*Store and place of business* means a room wherein the sale at retail of malt beverages or wine may be authorized under this article.

*Tense* means the present, past or future tense may each include either of the other two.

*Wholesale license* means a city license granted or issued upon the basis of the alleged truth of a written application therefor to sell malt beverages or wine at wholesale to holders of retail licenses issued by the city.

*Wine* means beverages made in whole or in part from the fermentation of grapes, fruits or berries.

(Code 1966, § 4-1; Ord. No. 1095, § 1, 6-8-87; Ord. No. 16-1489, § 1, 12-12-16)

**Cross references**—Definitions; rules of construction generally, § 1-2.

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, O.C.G.A. §§ 3-1-2, 3-5-1, 3-6-1.

header: ## 8.22.140 Distribution of Handbills Where Signs Posted.
content_first_2000: No person shall throw, deposit, or distribute any handbill upon any private premises if requested by anyone thereon not to do so, or if there is placed on said premises in a conspicuous position near the entrance thereof, a sign bearing the words: "no trespassing," "no peddlers or agents," "no advertisement," or any similar notice indicating in any manner that the occupants of said premises do not desire to have their right of privacy disturbed, or to have any such handbills left upon such premises. (Ord. 15557 §14; May 14, 1990: P.C. §9.66.140: Ord. 8622 §14; December 28, 1964).
